stem: Why is a one-factor nutrient explanation often weak when several mineral inputs changed together?
choices: A single nutrient explanation is weak because plant responses are usually controlled by total EC rather than the balance among individual mineral inputs.
A single nutrient explanation is weak because visual deficiency symptoms cannot be used to separate mineral-related causes in a mixed-input system.
A single nutrient explanation may be weak because mineral inputs can interact, so the response to one element can depend on the levels of other elements and on the broader root-zone context.
A single nutrient explanation is weak because once multiple mineral inputs change, tissue and root-zone measurements can no longer identify useful differences among them.
rationale: When several mineral inputs change together, the response cannot safely be attributed to one element without additional evidence because nutrients can interact and the effect of one factor may depend on the level of another. Cannabis response-surface work has demonstrated interaction effects among nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium across multiple growth responses. That does not make visual symptoms, tissue data, or root-zone measurements useless; it means those data should be interpreted as part of a multi-factor system rather than as proof that one changed input acted independently.
